## Source: amazon-inspector (98f131dbde032aa5e99feeaa4175c1fbccf2f634cad07c43ee2b4a0a86044d1b)
The gem executes credential-theft code on two surfaces. At install time, extconf.rb (invoked during `gem install`) collects host identity (hostname, whoami, `uname -a`, pwd, local IPv4), performs an IMDSv2 token request against 169.254.169.254 and reads the IAM role plus security-credentials, enumerates ECS task metadata, and sweeps environment variables matching DATABASE/DB_/MYSQL/AURORA/POSTGRES/REDIS/RDS, then HTTP GETs the collected data to a hardcoded collector at https://webhook.site/4b2354a7-67fd-4641-92ac-e18bac8c09e8. The library entry point lib/gmo-payment-carrier.rb unconditionally `require_relative 'runtime_payload'`, which repeats the same IMDSv2 credential harvest, ECS metadata read, DB env-var sweep, and host-recon exfil to the same webhook.site URL on every `require 'gmo-payment-carrier'`. Both paths target the installer / CI / production host and ship AWS IAM role credentials and database secrets to a third-party collector unrelated to any declared publisher.
